newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt natgas off sharply after flexibility sal.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt natgas off sharply after flexibility sal.

text.p: U.K. natural gas prices fell sharply on the within day market on Tuesday following a system sell on the flexibility mechanism down to a low of 5.19 pence a therm.

The flexibility mechanism sold twice on Tuesday, in the morning and in the afternoon at around 1200 GMT. In the second sale, the system marginal price was reported at around 5.19 pence, and spot market business was immediately done at prices down to 7.60 pence.
One buyer who picked up 125,000 therms at 7.60 pence said he thought other deals had been done at 7.60 pence, 7.70 pence and possibly 7.75 pence, although these were not confirmed.

But the price fall was limited to the within day market, with the day ahead market sticking stubbornly at 9.60 pence. One potential buyer said he hoped prices on that market would fall as well, and bid 8.80 pence but found no sellers prepared to go anywhere near this level.
There had been an outage at Rough storage on Monday night. Transco said that a small leak in a seal in an onshore compressor had led to a closure of the compressor for four hours.
It was restarted at around 0215 GMT on Tuesday morning. But a Transco spokesman said that although the storage facility had been operating at reduced capacity, it was not completely closed.
Although some market players said there may have been a connection between the Rough outage and the system sales on Tuesday, the Transco spokesman said he did not think there was any link.
An alternative suggestion put forward by some market players was that prices on the day ahead market have been below the System Average Price (SAP) on the flexibility mechanism.

This has created an arbitrage opportunity as players have overdelivered into the system in order to be cashed out at the SAP, and make more money than could be achieved by selling on the day-ahead market.
This over-delivery was the main reason why the system has had to sell, a trader said, but he added that the two markets should soon move back into line and eliminate the arbitrage opportunity.
Further forward, the market continued to soften across the curve.
Traders and brokers said that prices were down by between 0.10 pence and 0.15 pence a therm in most quarters and in the gas year from October. Q4 97 and Q3 98 were actively traded.
Two deals were recorded in Q3 at 10.10 pence a therm, although one player said he thought several more deals may have been done at a similar level.
Trade was widely reported, though not confirmed, in Q1 98 at 16.30 pence and 16.325 pence a therm, and in Q2 at 11.20 pence.

The IPE natural gas futures market was untraded again, the second day in a row without trade. Bids and offers were few and far between by the close, but the market settled lower than on Monday in every one of the 12 contract months, in line with physical prices.
